competitors.positioning: They rent you a platform; we build one you own. No per-developer pricing, no vendor lock-in, complete customization, full data ownership.
competitors.response: SaaS IDP vendors solve the quick-launch problem but create the same lock-in you're trying to escape. We build on Backstage and open source running on your infrastructure—you own the stack permanently.

competitors.when_mentioned: When prospect compares to Container Solutions, Fullstaq, or similar K8s-focused firms
competitors.positioning: They'll help you build Kubernetes. We build the full IDP from Git push to production—including GitLab, Grafana, Backstage, and all platform services your developers actually touch.
competitors.response: Kubernetes is the foundation layer. The 80% surrounding it—CI/CD, observability, developer portal, security—is what makes it an Internal Developer Platform. We own the complete stack.

competitors.when_mentioned: When prospect considers Giant Swarm or similar managed K8s offerings
competitors.positioning: They operate Kubernetes clusters. We build and operate the entire IDP on open source infrastructure with guaranteed knowledge transfer.
competitors.response: Managed Kubernetes solves cluster operations but leaves you responsible for the platform services layer. We operate the complete IDP stack and transfer capability to your team—no long-term dependency.

competitors.when_mentioned: When discussing team composition or engagement quality.
competitors.positioning: We embed senior engineers immediately; they use juniors to learn on your dime.
competitors.response: You'll never get junior consultants learning on your time. Our engineers embed with your team from day one.

competitors.when_mentioned: When prospects compare vendor transparency and team depth.
competitors.positioning: They polish the brand while hiding the team. We put our co-founders front and center.
competitors.response: Our co-founders build the thing they sell. You can see their work and their history on their profiles.

competitors.when_mentioned: When the prospect says 'Security won't let us connect APIs' or 'We can't install agents.'
competitors.positioning: These tools fail when API access is blocked by security policy; we succeed by accepting any input tier.
competitors.response: Most tools require full access to work. We start with what you have—billing CSVs, state files, even answers—and only escalate if a gap materially changes the recommendation.

competitors.when_mentioned: When prospects mention having audit reports or risk scores that sit on a shelf.
competitors.positioning: They quantify the problem but don't prescribe the sequence of solution.
competitors.response: Scores tell you what's wrong; we tell you which lock to pick first and why.

competitors.when_mentioned: When prospects equate GDPR compliance with cloud sovereignty.
competitors.positioning: They sell legal comfort; we sell engineering reality.
competitors.response: GDPR compliance is not sovereignty. You can be compliant and still be locked in. We prove independence with architecture, not contracts.
